question: 9. Let $x=(x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n)$, $y=(y_1,y_2,\ldots,y_n)$, where $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n,y_1,y_2,\ldots,y_n$ are real numbers. We write $x>y$, if for some $k$, $1\le k\le(n-1)$, $x_1=y_1,x_2=y_2,\ldots,x_k=y_k$, but $x_{k+1}>y_{k+1}$. Show that for $u=(u_1,\ldots,u_n)$, $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_n)$, $w=(w_1,\ldots,w_n)$ and $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$, if $u>v$ and $w>z$, then $(u+w)>(v+z)$.

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
